tools.name: request_contact
tools.description: Sends a project inquiry or question to the Developh team with the person's own name, email and message. It writes: it creates an inquiry and emails the person a confirmation. The team usually replies by email within 2 to 8 business hours. Requires confirmed=true, which records that the person review

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: run_website_audit · Private data: request_contact · Public sink: request_contact · Destructive: run_website_audit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: run_website_audit · Private data: request_contact · Public sink: request_contact · Destructive: run_website_audit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_case_studies" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Published client work by Developh with links to each case study. Filter by sector (restaurants, tourism, clinics) or service (websites, online stores, branding, web apps) to get what was built in each case; with no filter, lists every published project." → after: "Published client work by Developh with links to each case study. Filter by sector (the ones with published cases so far; a missing sector means no case is published yet, not that the studio does not take it on) or service (websites, online stores, branding, web apps) to get what was built in each ca"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
